title: Money Can't Buy Happiness, But... Café Curtis
trend: TikTok/Instagram 'Money can't buy happiness, but...' (finish the phrase with a small luxury such as a coffee; Pepper Agency Nov 2026 TikTok and Instagram list, US) + holiday coffee drink first-sip taste tests (#holidaydrinks hashtag up 14%, 57M views, howtogoviral US weekly list, Nov 2026) — Denise films her first-sip review of the seven-dollar holiday mocha every morning; frugal Curtis opens 'Café Curtis' in the kitchen to save money, buying a frother, twelve syrups and a giant espresso machine while the old coffee maker gets jealous; twist: his spreadsheet shows he spent four thousand dollars to save seven, and the holiday cup reveals he has been sneaking to the coffee shop every morning at six for 'research', where they call him Peppermint Kurt with a K

youtube_title: Money Can't Buy Happiness, But... Dad Opens A Coffee Shop | Funny Family Cartoon
description:
Denise says money can't buy happiness, but it can buy a holiday mocha. Curtis says that is seven dollars and forty cents, and opens his own coffee shop in the kitchen to save money.
The old coffee maker is not happy about it.

#cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #coffee
tiktok_caption: money can't buy happiness, but it can buy a seven dollar mocha. dad disagrees. #cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #coffee

lines.text: Money can't buy happiness.
But it can buy a large peppermint mocha with extra whip.
That cup was seven dollars and forty cents.
Limited edition, darling. I am only here until January.
It tastes like a snow day where nobody needs anything from me.
It tastes like seven dollars and forty cents leaving the house.
I make coffee for free. Nobody films me.
Drip, you make brown water and you beep at me.
The beep is love. I have beeped since two thousand nine.
That is it. Starting today, we have our own coffee shop.
Welcome to Café Curtis. Open daily. Located right here by the toaster.
Plain coffee. One candy cane. I stir it with the candy cane.
First sip review. It tastes like a hallway.
Okay. Café Curtis needs to grow. I made a small investment.
Money can't buy happiness, but it can buy a milk frother.
That is my line. You cannot use my line.
So I am being replaced by a whisk with a battery.
Also twelve syrups. Peppermint, gingerbread, and one called winter.
What flavor is winter?
I don't know. It was on sale. It tastes a little like a candle.
The foam is on the ceiling, Curtis.
First sip review. It tastes like a candle that went to college.
That is progress. Yesterday it was a hallway.
Big news. Café Curtis just got a real espresso machine.
Curtis. It is the size of our car.
It has a steering wheel for the steam. It is very Italian.
Where am I supposed to live now?
The garage, buddy. Next to the lawn mower. You two will love each other.
The lawn mower does not beep. The lawn mower screams.
How much did all of this cost?
Do not worry. I made a spreadsheet. We are saving so much money.
Frother, forty dollars. Syrups, ninety. Chef hat, sixty.
Espresso machine, three thousand nine hundred dollars.
Total, four thousand and ninety. Savings so far, seven dollars and forty cents.
We break even in only one and a half years. If you drink eight a day.
There is one more thing. I was not going to say it.
I know this man. He comes to my shop every morning at six.
Every morning? Curtis!
That was research. A café owner has to study the competition.
The whole staff knows him. They call him Peppermint Kurt. With a K.
So you were drinking the seven dollar mocha every day too.
Two. One for the drive. One to take notes.
And at night he comes to the garage and drinks me. Black. Crying.
Drip! That was between us!
New plan. Café Curtis is open to the whole street.
Seven dollars and forty cents a cup. The neighbors are already outside.
Money can't buy happiness. But it can buy back an espresso machine.
Remember, I am limited edition. I leave in January.
I have been here since two thousand nine. I am unlimited edition.
First sip review. Drip, you taste like home.
Beep.
